verdict.summary: Notion's OAuth is simple: a public connection gets OAuth, and users choose which pages to share instead of granting scopes. The decision that matters is installation scope, 'Any workspace' or 'Selected workspaces', which is permanent. A Marketplace listing is optional and reviewed in 5-10 business days. One step is unclear: Notion's docs say the Authorization URL appears after a public connection is 'submitted for review', but don't say what that review involves.
verdict.approval_wait: none documented for OAuth use; Marketplace listing 5-10 business days

gates.name: Public connection in your workspace
gates.unlocks: You can authorize your own workspace and pick the pages the connection can access.
limits: Access is page-by-page: users share specific pages and databases.

gates.name: Selected workspaces
gates.unlocks: A public connection limited to a set of workspaces chosen at creation.
limits: Installation scope can't be changed after creation.
Selected-workspace connections can't be listed on the Marketplace.

gates.name: Any workspace (optionally listed)
gates.unlocks: Any Notion workspace can install via OAuth. Public connections work without a Marketplace listing; listing adds discoverability.
limits: Marketplace listing is reviewed by Notion (5-10 business days).
gates.time_to_reach: immediately for OAuth (unconfirmed); 1-2 weeks to be listed

steps.title: Choose installation scope: Any workspace or Selected workspaces
steps.detail: Pick 'Any workspace' if you might ever list on the Marketplace or sell broadly. This can't be changed later.
gotchas: Selected-workspace connections are not eligible for the Marketplace.

steps.title: Create a public connection
steps.detail: In Notion's integrations page, create a new public connection and fill out the form, including the redirect URI(s).

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The integrations page renders only with JavaScript and requires sign-in.

steps.title: Submit the connection and copy the OAuth credentials
steps.detail: Notion's docs show the Authorization URL appearing after the public connection is submitted for review. Copy the OAuth client ID and secret into a Composio auth config for Notion (OAuth2).
gotchas: If the connection shows a pending review state, note how long it takes. This guide could not confirm it.

steps.title: Connect and test page selection
steps.detail: Authorize through Composio. Users choose pages in Notion's page picker, so an agent can verify which pages the token can actually read and warn when nothing has been shared.
gotchas: A successful connection with zero shared pages is the most common 'it doesn't work' report.

steps.title: Optional: prepare a Marketplace listing
steps.detail: An agent can draft the listing name, description, category, tags, images and logo. Listing details are managed separately from the connection.

steps.title: Optional: submit the listing and wait
steps.detail: Submit from the Connections listing page; Notion replies by email within 5-10 business days.

requirements.detail: Only these connections can be listed.

scopes.effect: Notion uses capabilities and per-page sharing instead of OAuth scopes; the consent prompt shows what the connection can do.

blockers.symptom: Connection succeeds but the agent sees no pages
blockers.cause: The user didn't share any pages in the page picker.
blockers.fix: Ask the user to reconnect and select pages, or add the connection to pages from the page menu.

blockers.symptom: Can't list the connection on the Marketplace
blockers.cause: It was created with 'Selected workspaces' scope.
blockers.fix: Create a new connection with 'Any workspace'. Scope can't be changed.

composio.note: Composio's managed Notion app works immediately. Your own connection mainly buys branding and control. Choose 'Any workspace' unless you only ever serve named customers.

evidence.claim: Public connections use OAuth, are installable in any workspace or selected workspaces (chosen at creation, can't be changed), and the form includes redirect URI(s).
evidence.quote: Fill out the form with your connection details, including your redirect URI(s)

evidence.claim: Notion uses a capabilities model and page-based access chosen by the user in a page picker.
Only public connections with 'Any workspace' scope can be listed on the Marketplace.
evidence.quote: Only public connections with an installation scope of Any workspace can be listed on the Marketplace.

evidence.claim: Marketplace listings are reviewed (reply within 5-10 business days); public connections work independently of listings and can be used via OAuth without being listed.
evidence.quote: After submission, expect to hear back from our team within 5-10 business days via email.

evidence.claim: Composio's Notion toolkit is managed (OAUTH2) with authorize URL https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize; it also supports API_KEY.
The integrations page exists but renders only with JavaScript.
evidence.quote: JavaScript must be enabled in order to use Notion.

evidence.claim: Notion's docs caption says the Authorization URL populates after a public connection is submitted for review.
evidence.quote: The Authorization URL field populates after a public connection is submitted for review

evidence.claim: Notion's authorize endpoint is reachable and redirects to an install-integration page.

open_questions: What does 'submitted for review' mean for a public connection that is not being listed? Is it an automatic step, or a human review that blocks other workspaces from installing? The docs don't say; hand-testing will settle it.
The required fields for the public connection form beyond redirect URIs (company name, website, privacy policy, terms, support email) are not listed in the pages we checked.
